diffuseAlbedo.note: A first colour for Qingbaishi (bluish-white dolomitic marble, Dashiwo, Fangshan): no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material.

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: Zhang et al. (2018), 'Thermally induced deterioration behaviour of two dolomitic marbles under heating-cooling cycles', Royal Society Open Science 5:180779, doi:10.1098/rsos.180779, Table 2, row QM-F (freshly quarried Qingbaishi marble, Dashiwo town, Fangshan district, Beijing). Read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6227961/
porosity.note: Confirmed. Table 2 gives the porosity of fresh QM as the fraction 0.019, with bulk density 2.824 g/cm3 and 99.7 % dolomite (0.3 % quartz). The value is high for a marble but it is measured on this stone. The dolomite result supports the proposer's point that refractiveIndex (1.6003, from calcite) should be derived again; that change is outside this batch.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Zhang et al. 2018, Royal Society Open Science 5:180779 (PMC6227961), text: average grain size of the minerals of QM 67.4 µm (HM, Hanbaiyu, 97.9 µm)
grain.note: Confirmed on the source. This is the mean crystal size of Dashiwo Qingbaishi, and it replaces the unverified 0.2 mm.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows: its bedding, veining or banding.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela, Renard, Klinger, Mair, Schmittbuhl & Brodsky (2012), 'Roughness of fault surfaces over nine decades of length scales', J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth 117, B08409, doi:10.1029/2011JB009041. Abstract read via Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1029/2011JB009041): H = 0.58 +/- 0.07 parallel and 0.81 +/- 0.04 perpendicular to slip, scales from 50 µm upward. The ipgp.fr PDF was fetched but its text could not be read.
hurst.note: The exponents and the arithmetic are confirmed from the abstract. I could not read section 4.1 details: the 41 patches, the limestone faults, mode I near 0.8, and independence from lithology. Cite the abstract only. This transfers a value from natural fault surfaces to a worked marble face.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
